name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: My wife is a vice principal at an elementary school, and most of my family works in education. I see up close how little time educators have to think about their own financial protection, which is why Horace Mann's focus on them stands out to me.

The Workplace Solutions Enablement role is about turning strategy into something a team and a channel can actually execute, and that has been the through-line of my career. At Wix, I led a team of 20 (later 8) on a new vertical that went from proof of concept to a profitable business line, building the process, training, and data standards it depended on. At Birdeye, I enabled a channel of 15 to 20 reseller partners to sell and support the product, and kept all but one. As a co-owner, I built compliance and operations systems from scratch in a state-regulated business. In each case, the work was the same: give a vague priority a structure, owners, and milestones, keep leaders informed on risks and tradeoffs, and make it repeatable.

I'll be direct about the gap: I haven't worked inside an insurance carrier or with Supplemental and Group products. I would bring the enablement and initiative leadership, and learn the product and distribution landscape quickly from the people who know it. I'd welcome a conversation.
